bib.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality

read.skipped: Proofs and derivations in Sections 3-5 and Appendices A-C were skimmed (theorem statements read, proofs not checked line by line); all of Sections 1, 2, 6-11 and Appendix D read.

question: How are structured state space models (Mamba) related to attention variants, and can that relation yield a faster, matmul-friendly SSM layer that stays competitive with Transformers?
hypothesis: SSMs and attention are closely related through structured (semiseparable) matrices, so Transformer algorithmic and systems optimisations can transfer to SSMs, giving a faster architecture (Mamba-2) with similar quality.
contributions: Equivalence between state space models and semiseparable matrices (Section 3)
Structured masked attention (SMA), a generalisation of linear attention (Section 4)
Structured state space duality (SSD): scalar-identity SSMs and 1-semiseparable SMA are duals with both linear and quadratic forms (Section 5)
A block-decomposition SSD algorithm using matrix multiplication (Section 6)
The Mamba-2 architecture: parallel projections, extra normalisation, head patterns (Section 7)
Systems work: tensor parallel, sequence parallel, variable length (Section 8)

method.summary: Theory linking SSMs, attention and semiseparable matrices, then a chunked SSD algorithm (diagonal blocks via quadratic form, off-diagonal low-rank blocks via states) and the Mamba-2 block. Mamba-2 models (125M-2.7B) are trained on the Pile and compared with Mamba, Transformer++ and open LMs; speed is benchmarked against Mamba's scan and FlashAttention-2.
method.task: autoregressive language modelling (next-token pretraining), zero-shot downstream evaluation, synthetic MQAR associative recall

results.claim: A dedicated SSD implementation is 2-8x faster than Mamba's optimized selective scan.
results.setup: A100 80GB PCIe, state dim 64 for left panel; Fig 10
results.quote: As a result, it is 2-8× faster than Mamba’s fused associative scan

results.claim: SSD is faster than FlashAttention-2 from sequence length 2K.
results.quote: Due to its linear scaling in sequence length, SSD is faster than FlashAttention-2 starting at sequence length 2𝐾.

results.claim: SSD is 6x faster than FlashAttention-2 at sequence length 16K.
results.quote: crossing over at sequence length 2K and 6× faster at sequence length 16K

results.claim: Mamba-2-2.7B reaches a higher zero-shot average than Mamba-2.8B and Pythia-2.8B.
results.setup: Pile, 300B tokens, GPT-NeoX tokenizer, EleutherAI harness, 7 tasks

results.claim: Mamba-2-2.7B Pile validation perplexity 6.09 vs Mamba-2.8B 6.22.
results.table: Table 1, row Mamba-2-2.7B, column Pile ppl

results.claim: Mamba-2 and Transformer++ have about the same average zero-shot accuracy at 2.7B; adding 6 attention layers (Mamba-2-Attention) improves it.
In a 350M 48-layer model, around 10% attention layers gives the best perplexity (6 attention blocks 8.26) vs pure Mamba-2 8.60 and Transformer++ 8.68.
results.setup: 350M, 48 layers, 7B tokens on the Pile, GPT-2 tokenizer
results.note: quote is my own assembly across lines; value 8.26 occurs in Table 2

results.claim: Multi-input (MVA) head pattern is far better than multi-query or multi-key patterns at equal state size.
results.setup: 125M models, 2.5B tokens, N=64, P=64: MIS 11.66 vs MQA 12.62 vs MKA 12.59
results.table: Table 5, top, row Multi-input (MIS), column Ppl.

results.claim: Parallel projections plus extra normalisation give the best block perplexity (Mamba-2 block 11.49 vs Mamba-1 block 11.76), and use fewer parameters (126.5M vs 129.3M).
results.table: Table 4, row Mamba-2 (Parallel, extra norm), column Perplexity

results.claim: MQAR: Mamba-2 performs significantly better than Mamba-1 even at equal state size N=16, and accuracy improves with N=64 and N=256.
results.setup: MQAR, T in {256,512,1024}, 2 layers, D in {32..256}; values read from Fig 8 not recorded
results.quote: Surprisingly, it is significantly better than Mamba-1 even when the state sizes are controlled (N = 16).

results.claim: Mamba-2 Pareto-dominates Mamba and Transformer++ in perplexity and wall-clock on Chinchilla scaling laws (about 125M-1.3B).
results.quote: Compared to our Transformer baseline, Mamba-2 is Pareto dominant on performance (perplexity), theoretical FLOPs, and actual wall-clock time.

results.claim: Kernel feature maps from linear attention (cosFormer, Performer, Based, ReBased) do not improve on simple pointwise activations.
results.quote: Overall, Table 6 and Table 7 found that the kernel approximation methods we tried did not seem to improve over simple pointwise non-linear activation functions for 𝜓.

results.claim: SSD training cost is O(TN^2) FLOPs, inference O(N^2) memory, versus attention T^2 N training FLOPs.
results.quote: There exists an algorithm for computing the model on any input 𝑋∈R(T,P) which only requires 𝑂(TN2) training FLOPs

results.claim: Any SSM of state size N on length T can be computed in O(TN) time.
results.quote: Any state space model (Definition 2.2) of state size N on sequence length T can be computed in time 𝑂(TN) (not accounting for potential preprocessing).

results.claim: Autoregressive SMA with bounded order must have a semiseparable mask L (efficient autoregressive attention is semiseparable SMA).
results.quote: the structured mask 𝐿must be a semiseparable matrix.

results.claim: Mamba-2 reduces tensor-parallel all-reduces per block from two to one.
results.setup: design argument, no measured training throughput given
results.quote: With Mamba-2, our goal is to have only one all-reduce per block, similar to attention or MLP blocks in Transformers.

limits: SSD restricts A to scalar times identity: 'trades off this expressivity for improved hardware efficiency'.
Whole-model training may be slower than a Transformer at short sequence length (about 2K) because a Mamba-2 model has L SSD layers versus L/2 attention plus L/2 MLP layers.
SSD does not generalise softmax attention or any attention kernel without a finite feature map.
Largest model 2.7B and 300B tokens; no multi-seed variance or significance tests; no compute (GPU-hours) or hardware for training reported.
Authors do not know which architectural change explains Mamba-2's MQAR gain over Mamba-1 at equal N.
Adding MLP layers reduced quality in the 2.7B hybrid comparison.
Hybrid comparisons: Mamba-2 (SSD only) matches Transformer++ rather than beating it.

terms.definition: State space models with scalar-identity structure on A and structured masked attention with 1-semiseparable mask are duals with the same linear and quadratic forms.
A generalisation of linear attention where a structured mask L multiplies the attention matrix, computed as a four-way tensor contraction.
A lower triangular matrix is N-semiseparable if every submatrix on or below the diagonal has rank at most N.
Head pattern with X per head and B, C shared across heads; analogue of multi-value attention; the pattern used by Mamba and Mamba-2.

(SSD Algorithm.) Block decomposition of the semiseparable matrix into diagonal (intra-chunk) and low-rank (inter-chunk) blocks.

figures.why: Block diagram contrasting Mamba and Mamba-2 blocks.

figures.why: Pareto comparison with Transformer++ and Mamba.

figures.caption: (Efficiency Benchmarks.) SSD is 2-8x faster than a Mamba fused scan and faster than FlashAttention-2 for sequence length 2k and above.
